items.plot: An honest Chicago police captain wages a stubborn campaign against a bootlegging gang boss who enjoys political protection. Their feud comes to a head when the gangster's kid brother and a nightclub singer get tangled in it.

items.title: 7th Heaven

won: Actress in a Leading Role — Janet Gaynor

items.plot: A brash Paris sewer worker shelters a mistreated young woman, and their reluctant arrangement in his rooftop garret blossoms into love. When World War I calls him to the front, faith in each other must sustain them.

items.title: Wings
items.plot: Two young men from the same small town, rivals for the same girl, become fighter pilots in World War I. Their friendship deepens through dogfights and furloughs in Paris, while the girl who loves one of them follows as an ambulance driver.

setting.place: Small-town America and the Western Front, France

items.title: Alibi

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Chester Morris

items.plot: A gangster just out of prison marries a police sergeant's daughter and uses her as cover while he plans more crimes. An undercover officer infiltrates his gang as the police close in on him for a murder.

items.title: In Old Arizona

won: Actor in a Leading Role — Warner Baxter

items.plot: A charming Mexican bandit known as the Cisco Kid robs stagecoaches across the Arizona Territory while an Army sergeant tries to catch him. Both men become involved with the same unfaithful woman, setting up a cunning act of revenge.

items.title: The Broadway Melody

nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Bessie Love

items.plot: Two sisters with a vaudeville act come to New York hoping to make it on Broadway. A song-and-dance man engaged to the older sister falls for the younger one, testing the sisters' loyalty.

items.title: Hollywood Revue
items.plot: MGM's early all-talking variety show strings together songs, dance numbers, comedy sketches, and novelty acts performed by the studio's stars. Highlights include a Technicolor Romeo and Juliet sendup and the debut of "Singin' in the Rain."

items.title: The Patriot

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Lewis Stone

items.plot: At the court of Russia's mad Tsar Paul I, his trusted adviser Count Pahlen decides the unstable ruler must be removed for the nation's sake, even though it means betraying a man who regards him as his only friend.

items.title: All Quiet on the Western Front
items.plot: Fired up by a patriotic teacher, a group of German schoolboys enlist in World War I. In the trenches they quickly learn the truth about combat, hunger, and death, and one young soldier comes to feel cut off from home.
items.source: All Quiet on the Western Front (Erich Maria Remarque)

items.title: The Big House

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Wallace Beery

items.plot: A young man convicted of manslaughter in a drunk-driving accident is thrown into a crowded prison cell with hardened criminals. Tensions rise behind the walls as a breakout is planned.

items.title: Disraeli

won: Actor in a Leading Role — George Arliss

items.plot: British Prime Minister Benjamin Disraeli schemes to buy control of the Suez Canal before Russia can. He outwits hostile politicians and foreign spies with help from his devoted wife and a young aristocratic couple.

items.title: The Divorcee

won: Actress in a Leading Role — Norma Shearer

items.plot: After learning that her husband has had a fling, a modern wife decides to have the same freedom he claims. Their marriage falls apart, and she enjoys being single for a while before she reconsiders what she wants.

items.title: The Love Parade

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Maurice Chevalier

items.plot: After a string of romantic scandals in Paris, a dashing count is called home to the kingdom of Sylvania, where he marries the young queen. He soon chafes at being a prince consort with nothing to do, and the royal marriage is strained.
items.source: Le Prince consort (Léon Xanrof and Jules Chancel)

setting.place: Paris and the fictional kingdom of Sylvania

items.title: Cimarron

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Richard Dix
Actress in a Leading Role — Irene Dunne

items.plot: A restless frontiersman joins the 1889 Oklahoma land rush and settles his family in a raw boomtown, where he starts a newspaper. Over four decades his wife builds a life and a career while his wanderlust keeps taking him away.

items.title: East Lynne
items.plot: An aristocratic wife is driven out of her marriage by a jealous sister-in-law and a misunderstanding, losing access to her child. Years of exile and hardship follow before she returns to the home she lost.

items.title: The Front Page

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Adolphe Menjou

items.plot: A star Chicago crime reporter wants to quit and get married, but his scheming editor will do anything to keep him on the job. An escaped death-row prisoner then gives them the scoop of the year.
items.source: The Front Page (Ben Hecht and Charles MacArthur)

items.title: Skippy

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Jackie Cooper

items.plot: Skippy, the mischievous son of a strict health inspector, befriends a poor boy from the shantytown across the tracks. The two boys try to raise money to save the friend's dog from the pound.

items.title: Trader Horn
items.plot: A veteran trader leads a safari through the African wilds with a young companion, looking for a missionary's long-lost daughter. They find her ruling a tribe and must escape with her across dangerous country.
items.source: Trader Horn (Alfred Aloysius Horn and Ethelreda Lewis)

items.title: Arrowsmith
items.plot: An idealistic young doctor wants to do medical research, but marriage, money, and ambition keep pulling him away from it. When he is sent to fight a plague in the West Indies, he must choose between science and compassion.

setting.place: American Midwest, New York, and the West Indies

items.title: Bad Girl
items.plot: A young working-class couple in New York meet, marry quickly, and expect a baby soon after. Pride and money worries lead each of them to misread the other, even though they deeply love each other.

items.title: The Champ

won: Actor in a Leading Role — Wallace Beery

items.plot: A washed-up boxer who drinks and gambles too much lives in Tijuana with his adoring young son. When the boy's wealthy mother comes back into his life, the Champ tries one more comeback to give his son something to be proud of.

items.title: Five Star Final
items.plot: A newspaper editor, under pressure to boost circulation, digs up a twenty-year-old murder scandal. The woman involved now lives a quiet, respectable life and her daughter is about to marry, so the story has devastating consequences.

items.title: Grand Hotel
items.plot: Over a few eventful days at a luxurious Berlin hotel, the guests' lives become entangled. They include a fading ballerina, a charming but broke baron, a struggling industrialist, his ambitious stenographer, and a dying clerk out to enjoy life.

items.title: One Hour with You
items.plot: A happily married Paris doctor and his wife are thrown into confusion when her flirtatious best friend sets her sights on him. Suspicions and misunderstandings multiply, and the husband sometimes addresses the audience directly.

items.title: Shanghai Express
items.plot: A notorious courtesan known as Shanghai Lily boards a train across war-torn China and finds her former lover, a British army doctor, among the passengers. Rebel forces seize the train, and their bond is put to a dangerous test.

setting.place: A train from Peking to Shanghai, China

items.title: The Smiling Lieutenant
items.plot: A Viennese officer winks at his violinist sweetheart during a royal parade, but the visiting princess thinks the wink was meant for her. To avoid a diplomatic incident he must marry the dowdy princess, who soon gets lessons in glamour from his former lover.

items.title: Cavalcade

nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Diana Wynyard

items.plot: Over three decades, the lives of a well-off London family and their servants are shaped by events such as the Boer War, Queen Victoria's death, the Titanic, and World War I. Through it all the families endure loss and change.

items.title: A Farewell to Arms
items.plot: An American ambulance driver serving with the Italian army in World War I falls in love with an English nurse. As the war drags on, they try to keep their love alive against separation and chaos.

items.title: 42nd Street
items.plot: A sick and nearly broke Broadway director pushes his cast hard to put on one last hit musical. When the leading lady breaks her ankle on the eve of opening, a chorus girl gets her big chance.

items.title: I Am a Fugitive from a Chain Gang

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Paul Muni

items.plot: A World War I veteran looking for a fresh start is wrongly caught up in a petty robbery and sentenced to a brutal Southern chain gang. His escape starts a long ordeal as a hunted man, even after he makes a respectable life for himself.
items.source: I Am a Fugitive from a Georgia Chain Gang! (Robert E. Burns)

items.title: Lady for a Day

nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — May Robson

items.plot: Apple Annie, a poor street vendor in New York, has convinced the daughter she raised in Spain that she is a wealthy society lady. When the daughter visits with her aristocratic fiancé, a superstitious gambler and his friends stage an elaborate deception to help.

items.title: Little Women
items.plot: While their father is away at the Civil War, four sisters grow up together in a modest New England home under their mother's care. Tomboyish Jo, who wants to be a writer, leads them through love, ambition, and heartbreak.

items.title: The Private Life of Henry VIII

won: Actor in a Leading Role — Charles Laughton

items.plot: England's much-married King Henry VIII goes from wife to wife after the execution of Anne Boleyn. Through banquets, court intrigues, and domestic squabbles, the film shows him as a lusty, comic, and lonely monarch.

items.title: She Done Him Wrong
items.plot: Lady Lou, a saloon singer in the 1890s Bowery, juggles a string of admirers, among them a jailed jewel thief, a crooked politician, and a handsome young temperance worker. He may not be what he seems.

items.title: Smilin' Through
items.plot: A bitter old Englishman, whose bride was killed on their wedding day decades earlier, raises his orphaned niece. When she falls for the son of the man responsible for that tragedy, the past threatens the young couple's happiness.
items.source: Smilin' Through (Jane Cowl and Jane Murfin)

items.title: State Fair
items.plot: An Iowa farm family goes to the state fair. The father hopes his prize hog wins, the mother enters her pickles and mincemeat, and their grown son and daughter each find a fleeting romance with a stranger.

items.title: The Barretts of Wimpole Street

nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Norma Shearer

items.plot: The poet Elizabeth Barrett is an invalid confined to her London home by a domineering, possessive father. When the poet Robert Browning starts writing to her and then visiting, she gains the strength to choose her own life.
items.source: The Barretts of Wimpole Street (Rudolf Besier)

items.title: Cleopatra
items.plot: After Caesar is assassinated, Egypt's queen Cleopatra seduces the Roman general Mark Antony to protect her throne and her country. Their love affair sets them against the might of Rome and Octavian.

items.title: Flirtation Walk
items.plot: A private stationed in Hawaii romances a general's daughter, then ends up at West Point, where she reappears as the general takes command. Cadet rivalry and the big academy show test their romance.

setting.place: Hawaii and West Point, New York

items.title: The Gay Divorcee

nominated: Music (Original Song Score Or Adaptation Score)

items.plot: A woman trying to get a divorce goes to an English seaside resort to stage an affair as evidence. She mistakes an American dancer who has been chasing her for the hired co-respondent, and he can't work out why she's suddenly so willing.
items.source: Gay Divorce (Dwight Taylor and Cole Porter)

setting.place: London and an English seaside resort

items.title: Here Comes the Navy
items.plot: A cocky riveter joins the Navy to get even with a chief petty officer who beat him in a fight, and then falls for the officer's sister. Aboard the USS Arizona and later on a dirigible, he has to earn his shipmates' respect.

setting.place: US Navy bases and ships, California

items.title: The House of Rothschild
items.plot: The Rothschild family's patriarch tells his five sons to set up banks in Europe's capitals to protect themselves from persecution. During the Napoleonic Wars, Nathan Rothschild in London risks the family fortune to finance the Allies while facing an antisemitic aristocrat.

items.title: Imitation of Life
items.plot: A widowed white mother and her Black housekeeper make a fortune with the housekeeper's pancake recipe. As their daughters grow up, the white daughter falls for her mother's fiancé, and the light-skinned Black daughter tries to pass as white and rejects her own mother.

setting.place: Atlantic City and New York City

items.title: It Happened One Night

won: Actor in a Leading Role — Clark Gable
Actress in a Leading Role — Claudette Colbert

items.plot: A runaway heiress escapes her father's yacht and boards a bus to New York to join the man she has just married. An out-of-work reporter recognizes her and offers to help in exchange for an exclusive story, and their bickering road trip turns into romance.

items.title: One Night of Love

won: Music (Original Song Score Or Adaptation Score)
nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Grace Moore

items.plot: An American singer who fails to win a radio contest goes to Italy to study opera. A demanding, famous voice teacher takes her on, and as she rises toward stardom their stormy partnership becomes romance.

items.title: The Thin Man

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — William Powell

items.plot: Nick Charles is a retired detective who would rather drink cocktails with his wealthy wife Nora. When an inventor disappears and a murder follows, the couple trade quips while drawing all the suspects together to find the killer.

items.title: Viva Villa!
items.plot: Pancho Villa sees his father flogged to death as a boy and grows up to be a bandit, then a revolutionary general. He fights alongside an idealistic leader to overthrow Mexico's dictatorship, and an American reporter follows his rise.
items.source: Viva Villa! (Edgcumb Pinchon and O.B. Stade)

items.title: The White Parade
items.plot: In 1907, a young woman enrolls at a demanding nursing school, hoping to follow Florence Nightingale's example. She falls for a wealthy playboy while working through rigorous training, and has to decide between marriage and her vocation.

setting.place: A US nursing school and hospital

items.title: Alice Adams

nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Katharine Hepburn

items.plot: In a small Midwestern town, a young woman from a family with little money tries hard to fit in with the wealthy set. When a well-to-do young man takes an interest in her, she keeps covering up her family's circumstances, and it goes badly at a disastrous dinner.

items.title: Broadway Melody of 1936
items.plot: A Broadway gossip columnist hungry for scandal goes after a producer by inventing a mysterious French star. Meanwhile, the producer's talented hometown sweetheart is trying to get into his new show.

items.title: Captain Blood

nominated: Music (Original Song Score Or Adaptation Score)

items.plot: An Irish doctor is wrongly convicted of treason for treating a wounded rebel and sold as a slave in the Caribbean. He leads his fellow convicts in a daring escape and becomes a feared pirate captain, while still in love with the planter's niece who once bought him.

items.title: David Copperfield
items.plot: Young David Copperfield's happy childhood ends when his widowed mother marries a cruel man. He grows up through hardship, kindness, and colorful acquaintances such as the debt-ridden Mr. Micawber, until he is grown and finding his way in Victorian England.

items.title: The Informer

won: Actor in a Leading Role — Victor McLaglen
Music (Original Song Score Or Adaptation Score)

items.plot: In Dublin during the Irish War of Independence, a desperate, hard-drinking ex-rebel informs on a friend to collect a reward. During one long, guilt-ridden night he squanders the money as his former comrades close in.

items.title: Les Miserables
items.plot: Jean Valjean, a convict jailed for stealing bread, rebuilds his life as a respected mayor after a bishop shows him mercy. The relentless police inspector Javert refuses to let him go, pursuing him for years across France.

items.title: The Lives of a Bengal Lancer

won: Assistant Director — Clem Beauchamp, Paul Wing

items.plot: On India's North-West Frontier, a seasoned Scottish-Canadian officer, a cocky newcomer, and their commander's unhappy son serve together in a British cavalry regiment. Rebel tribesmen are plotting an uprising, and the three are drawn into a daring and dangerous mission.

items.title: A Midsummer Night's Dream
items.plot: Over one enchanted night in an Athenian forest, four young lovers are tangled up by fairy mischief, and a fairy queen falls for a weaver with a donkey's head. The production uses lavish effects and Mendelssohn's music.

items.title: Mutiny on the Bounty

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Clark Gable
Actor in a Leading Role — Charles Laughton
Actor in a Leading Role — Franchot Tone
Music (Original Song Score Or Adaptation Score)

items.plot: On a voyage to Tahiti, the crew of HMS Bounty suffer under the brutal Captain Bligh. His first officer, Fletcher Christian, is pushed to the breaking point and leads a mutiny that changes the lives of everyone on board.
writers: Charles Nordhoff and James Norman Hall (novel)
items.source: Mutiny on the Bounty (Charles Nordhoff and James Norman Hall)

setting.place: HMS Bounty, Tahiti and the South Pacific

items.title: Naughty Marietta
items.plot: To escape an arranged marriage, a French princess disguises herself as a girl being sent to colonial Louisiana to find a husband. Pirates attack the ship, and a dashing mercenary captain rescues her and wins her heart in song.
items.source: Naughty Marietta (Victor Herbert and Rida Johnson Young)

items.title: Ruggles of Red Gap
items.plot: A proper English valet is lost in a poker game in Paris and ends up serving a rowdy American couple in a Western frontier town. In egalitarian Red Gap he is mistaken for a gentleman and starts to discover his own independence.
items.source: Ruggles of Red Gap (Harry Leon Wilson)

items.title: Top Hat
items.plot: An American dancer in London falls for a woman whose hotel room is right below his. She mistakes him for her friend's husband, and the misunderstanding follows them to Venice, with Irving Berlin songs and dance numbers along the way.

items.title: Anthony Adverse

Actress in a Supporting Role — Jessica Chastain

items.title: Beasts of the Southern Wild

items.source: Les Misérables (stage musical, from Victor Hugo's novel)

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Bradley Cooper

Actress in a Supporting Role — Jacki Weaver

items.title: American Hustle

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Christian Bale
Actor in a Supporting Role — Bradley Cooper
Actress in a Leading Role — Amy Adams
Actress in a Supporting Role — Jennifer Lawrence

items.title: Nebraska

Actress in a Supporting Role — June Squibb

items.plot: An aging, stubborn Montana man is convinced he has won a sweepstakes prize in Nebraska. His weary son agrees to drive him there, and the trip stops in his old hometown, where family and old acquaintances come out of the past.

items.title: Philomena

items.source: The Lost Child of Philomena Lee

items.title: American Sniper

Actor in a Supporting Role — Edward Norton
Actress in a Supporting Role — Emma Stone

items.title: The Theory of Everything

nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Felicity Jones

items.source: Travelling to Infinity: My Life with Stephen

items.title: The Big Short

nominated: Actor in a Supporting Role — Tom Hardy

items.title: Tár

nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Cate Blanchett

items.plot: Lydia Tár, a celebrated conductor at the top of the classical music world, is preparing a career-defining Mahler recording in Berlin. Her controlling behavior and past choices start to catch up with her, and her carefully built world begins to fall apart.

items.title: Triangle of Sadness
items.plot: A celebrity model couple are invited on a luxury cruise with super-rich passengers. The voyage becomes a disaster, and when some of the guests are stranded, the class order is turned upside down. A savage satire of wealth, beauty and power.

setting.place: A luxury yacht and an island

items.title: Women Talking
items.plot: In an isolated religious colony, the women learn that the men have been drugging and assaulting them at night for years. While the men are away, they meet in a hayloft and argue over whether to stay and fight, do nothing, or leave.

items.title: American Fiction

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Jeffrey Wright
Actor in a Supporting Role — Sterling K. Brown

items.plot: A frustrated Black novelist and professor is tired of a publishing world that only rewards stereotyped Black stories. He writes an over-the-top, cliché-filled novel under a pen name as a joke, and it becomes a huge hit while he deals with family troubles at home.

items.title: Anatomy of a Fall

nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Sandra Hüller

items.plot: A man is found dead in the snow outside his family's remote chalet in the French Alps, and his wife, a successful writer, is accused of killing him. Her trial puts their marriage under scrutiny, and their partially blind son is the one key witness.

items.title: Barbie

nominated: Actor in a Supporting Role — Ryan Gosling
Actress in a Supporting Role — America Ferrera

items.plot: Stereotypical Barbie lives a perfect life in Barbieland until she suddenly starts having thoughts about death and finds her feet have gone flat. She and Ken travel to the real world, where they each run into some uncomfortable discoveries about themselves and about society.

items.title: The Holdovers

won: Actress in a Supporting Role — Da'Vine Joy Randolph
nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Paul Giamatti

items.plot: Over Christmas break in 1970, a gruff, unpopular classics teacher at a New England boarding school has to supervise a troubled student who has nowhere to go. The grieving head cook stays with them, and the three form an unlikely bond.

items.title: Killers of the Flower Moon

nominated: Actor in a Supporting Role — Robert De Niro
Actress in a Leading Role — Lily Gladstone

items.plot: In 1920s Oklahoma, oil makes members of the Osage Nation rich, and they start being murdered one after another. A returning war veteran marries an Osage woman while doing the bidding of his scheming uncle. The killings eventually bring in the young FBI.
items.source: Killers of the Flower Moon: The Osage Murders and the Birth of the FBI

items.title: Maestro

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Bradley Cooper
Actress in a Leading Role — Carey Mulligan

items.plot: A portrait of composer and conductor Leonard Bernstein, from his overnight breakthrough to his fame. It focuses on his decades-long, complicated marriage to actress Felicia Montealegre and the strain that his ambition and his relationships with men put on it.

items.title: Oppenheimer

won: Actor in a Leading Role — Cillian Murphy
Actor in a Supporting Role — Robert Downey Jr.
nominated: Actress in a Supporting Role — Emily Blunt

items.plot: Physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer leads the secret Manhattan Project at Los Alamos to build the atomic bomb during World War II. Years later, a security hearing driven by politics and old rivalries examines his loyalties and the moral weight of what he made.

setting.place: Los Alamos, Berkeley, Washington D.C. and Europe

items.title: Past Lives
items.plot: Childhood sweethearts Nora and Hae Sung are separated when her family emigrates from Seoul. Decades later they reconnect online, and eventually he visits her in New York, where she now lives with her husband. They face the lives they might have had.

items.title: Poor Things

won: Actress in a Leading Role — Emma Stone
nominated: Actor in a Supporting Role — Mark Ruffalo

items.plot: Bella Baxter, a young woman brought back to life by an unorthodox scientist, has an adult body and a child's mind. Eager to experience the world, she runs off on a wild trip across Europe with a slippery lawyer and grows quickly into a free-thinking, independent woman.

items.title: The Zone of Interest
items.plot: Auschwitz commandant Rudolf Höss and his wife Hedwig try to build an ideal family life in their house and garden right next to the camp wall. The horror on the other side is mostly heard rather than seen, which makes its presence more chilling.

items.title: Anora

won: Actress in a Leading Role — Mikey Madison
nominated: Actor in a Supporting Role — Yura Borisov

items.plot: Ani, a Brooklyn stripper, impulsively marries the reckless son of a Russian oligarch in Las Vegas. When his parents find out, they send their fixers to get the marriage annulled, and a chaotic night chase across New York follows.

items.title: The Brutalist

won: Actor in a Leading Role — Adrien Brody
nominated: Actor in a Supporting Role — Guy Pearce
Actress in a Supporting Role — Felicity Jones

items.plot: László Tóth, a visionary Hungarian Jewish architect who survived the Holocaust, emigrates to postwar America to start over. A wealthy industrialist offers him a huge commission that could define his career, but the patronage comes with a high price.

items.title: A Complete Unknown

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Timothée Chalamet
Actor in a Supporting Role — Edward Norton
Actress in a Supporting Role — Monica Barbaro

items.plot: In 1961 a 19-year-old Bob Dylan arrives in Greenwich Village with a guitar and a few songs. He quickly rises through the folk scene to fame. His restlessness builds up to a disputed move to electric rock at the 1965 Newport Folk Festival.

setting.place: New York City and Newport, Rhode Island

items.title: Conclave

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Ralph Fiennes
Actress in a Supporting Role — Isabella Rossellini

items.plot: After the Pope dies unexpectedly, Cardinal Lawrence has to run the secret conclave that will choose his successor. Behind the Vatican's locked doors, ambitions, plots and buried scandals come out, and Lawrence finds himself caught up in them.

items.title: Dune: Part Two
items.plot: Paul Atreides joins Chani and the Fremen to fight back against the conspirators who destroyed his family. As his visions get darker and his followers start to see him as a messiah, he has to choose between the woman he loves and the fate of the universe.

items.title: Emilia Pérez

won: Actress in a Supporting Role — Zoe Saldaña
nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Karla Sofía Gascón

items.plot: Rita, an overworked Mexican lawyer, gets a secret offer from a feared cartel boss: help him disappear for good and start a new life as a woman. Years later the past comes back. A Spanish-language crime musical.

items.title: I'm Still Here

nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Fernanda Torres

items.plot: In 1970s Rio de Janeiro, under Brazil's military dictatorship, former congressman Rubens Paiva is taken away by the regime and never returns. His wife Eunice has to hold the family together while she fights for the truth about what happened to him.

setting.place: Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, Brazil

items.title: Nickel Boys
items.plot: In Jim Crow-era Florida, Elwood, a bright and idealistic Black teenager, is wrongly sent to a brutal reform school. There he becomes close friends with the more cynical Turner. Shot entirely from the two boys' first-person points of view.

items.title: The Substance

nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Demi Moore

items.plot: Elisabeth Sparkle, a fading TV fitness star fired for getting older, takes a black-market drug that creates a younger, "better" version of herself. The two have to share one life under strict rules, and things go grotesquely wrong when they stop following them.

items.title: Wicked

nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Cynthia Erivo
Actress in a Supporting Role — Ariana Grande

items.plot: Long before Dorothy arrives in Oz, Elphaba, a misunderstood young woman with green skin, becomes the unlikely roommate of the popular Galinda at Shiz University. Their rivalry grows into friendship until a meeting with the Wizard changes both their futures.

items.title: Bugonia

nominated: Actress in a Leading Role — Emma Stone

items.plot: Two conspiracy-obsessed cousins kidnap the powerful CEO of a pharmaceutical company. They are convinced she is an alien who plans to destroy Earth. Holding her captive in their basement, they begin a tense battle of wills. A darkly comic remake of a Korean cult film.

items.title: F1
items.plot: Sonny Hayes was a 1990s Formula One prodigy before a crash ended his career. Decades later he is persuaded to come back and drive for a struggling team alongside a gifted, cocky rookie, with one last chance to prove himself.

items.title: Frankenstein

nominated: Actor in a Supporting Role — Jacob Elordi

items.plot: Brilliant, arrogant scientist Victor Frankenstein brings a creature to life out of dead bodies and then rejects what he has made. The film tells both creator and creature's sides as their bitter bond leads them across Europe and into the Arctic ice.

items.title: Hamnet

won: Actress in a Leading Role — Jessie Buckley

items.plot: In Elizabethan England, the free-spirited Agnes marries a young Latin tutor who later goes off to London to write plays. When the plague hits their family in Stratford, their grief threatens the marriage and goes on to shape one of the most famous plays ever written.

items.title: Marty Supreme

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Timothée Chalamet

items.plot: Marty Mauser is a brash young table-tennis hustler in 1950s New York who is sure he will become a world champion. He schemes, lies and gambles his way toward greatness, and the chase takes him from the Lower East Side to London and Tokyo.

setting.place: New York City, London and Tokyo

items.title: One Battle after Another

won: Actor in a Supporting Role — Sean Penn
nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Leonardo DiCaprio
Actor in a Supporting Role — Benicio Del Toro
Actress in a Supporting Role — Teyana Taylor

items.plot: Years after his days as a revolutionary, a burned-out ex-militant lives off the grid with his teenage daughter. When an old enemy suddenly comes back into their lives, he has to pull himself together and fight his way through a chaotic chase to protect her.

items.title: The Secret Agent

nominated: Actor in a Leading Role — Wagner Moura

items.plot: In 1977, during Brazil's military dictatorship, a technology expert running from a mysterious past goes to Recife at Carnival time hoping to rebuild his life. He soon finds that the danger he fled is closing in on him. A political thriller full of period atmosphere.

items.title: Sentimental Value

nominated: Actor in a Supporting Role — Stellan Skarsgård
Actress in a Leading Role — Renate Reinsve
Actress in a Supporting Role — Elle Fanning
Actress in a Supporting Role — Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas

items.plot: Two sisters in Oslo, one a stage actress, see their long-absent father again after their mother dies. He is a once-celebrated film director who wants to shoot a comeback movie in the family home, and he offers the lead role to his estranged daughter.

items.title: Sinners

won: Actor in a Leading Role — Michael B. Jordan
nominated: Actor in a Supporting Role — Delroy Lindo
Actress in a Supporting Role — Wunmi Mosaku

items.plot: In 1932 Mississippi, twin brothers Smoke and Stack come home from Chicago with money to open a juke joint for the local Black community. On opening night the blues draws in more than paying customers, and an evil arrives that threatens everyone inside.

items.title: Train Dreams
items.plot: Robert Grainier, a logger and railroad laborer, lives a quiet life in the American Northwest as the country changes rapidly around him. After a devastating loss, he looks for meaning in the wilderness. A meditative portrait of one ordinary man's life.
